A run gets a generated `hrun_*` identity and an immutable root under `.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`.\n\nSubmit writes immutable/spec-bound state atomically: `spec.json`, digest-only `owner.json`, 0600 one-shot `input.cap` and `input.prompt`, initial `snapshot.json`, and append-only `events.jsonl`. Provider output updates a separate `lastProviderProgressAt` only when observable; unsupported observability is represented as `unobservable`, never fabricated.\n\nA terminal is created exclusively and exactly once. It records outcome, timing, exit/timeout/cancel reason, provider identity, spec/profile binding digests, evidence journal digest, process cleanup facts, residual process state and an independent `replacementSafe`. Repeated status/cancel/attach calls first acquire a short `reconcile.lock`, re-read facts, and materialize terminal truth for deadline expiry or authoritative worker/provider death. Silence is never a transition predicate. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity yields honest residual `unknown` and `replacementSafe:false`, not blind termination.\n\nInitial RED tests cover: exclusive claim winner, unchanged running state across silent intervals, worker crash followed by deadline reconciliation, one terminal under concurrent reconcilers, idempotent status/cancel, terminal/result digest stability, capability/prompt deletion, and no automatic retry.\n\n## CHK-002 — Expose submit, attach, status and cancel command surfaces\n\nExtend the host-run command schema:\n- `host_run --detach` submits, waits only for a bounded claim handshake, and returns `runId/state/deadlineAt/generation`;\n- foreground `host_run` calls the same submit path then attaches to that run, projecting live output and final usage without owning the provider child;\n- `host_run_status --runId ... --waitMs ...` performs bounded long-poll, returning immediately on terminal or snapshot-generation change and otherwise after at most 30000ms;\n- `host_run_cancel --runId ... --reason ...` writes an idempotent cooperative request and reconciles;\n- hidden `host_run_worker --runId ...` is runtime-only and never advertised as an operator workflow.\n\nDeclare command policy, process-fact level and CLI watchdog behavior for runtime continuation. JSON stdout remains one machine object; text mode keeps live stream routing and concise status guidance. The handler never stores raw prompt/capability in argv or durable public artifacts.\n\nRED starts at CLI/handler seams: detach returns after claim, status wait is capped, foreground and detached share one run/receipt shape, cancel is idempotent, unknown run is fail-closed, and caller termination leaves the run queryable.\n\n## CHK-003 — Supervise provider processes portably and honestly\n\nProvider adapters remain private to ManagedHostRun and preserve canonical launcher specifications. Preserve finite total timeout/deadline, bounded output projection, provider usage candidate extraction, turn-failure diagnostic, passthrough-degradation honesty and failure classification. It runs focused managed lifecycle, command, real process-group, admission, cross-host and receipt-gate tests. Add bounded mutation bites that prove premature silence failure, terminal-only monitoring and forged receipt changes are caught. Avoid destructive shared-dist mutations during parallel review.\n\nRegister host-run runtime artifacts with gitignore/material-hash/repair semantics. `doctor`/status diagnostics distinguish worker liveness, provider progress observability, deadline, cancel state, residuals, replacement safety and retention. +## Shared provider admission
+
+Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
+of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
+token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
+Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
+not process admission.
+
+A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
+reclaimable; corrupt/ownerless slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release
+checks the acquire token so a late old holder cannot delete a slot that has
+already been reclaimed and reassigned.
+
+Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
+admission. Readiness/version probes are classified separately and do not become
+review evidence.
+
+### Provider execution surface classification
+
+Every production provider spawn site is classified by
+`ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus` (`packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts`),
+and `packages/main/src/tasks/provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts` fails if a
+new spawn path appears without one:
+
+| Status | Meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `managed` | Executes through ManagedHostRun: durable run identity, supervised process group, absolute deadline, exactly one terminal receipt. |
+| `admission_only` | Not managed-executed, but routed through the shared provider admission boundary, so the concurrency cap and slot accounting still apply. |
+| `adapter_only` | A low-level adapter module whose *caller* owns admission; the adapter itself makes no gate claim. |
+| `readiness_probe` | Version/readiness probing only. Never becomes review evidence. |
+| `legacy_unmanaged` | A provider spawn that is neither managed nor admission-routed. **Reserved, and currently empty by contract.** |
+
+`admission_managed` is not a status value: admission and managed execution are
+two separate properties, expressed by `admission_only` (admission without
+managed execution) and `managed` (both).
+
+The `legacy_unmanaged` bucket exists so an unmanaged spawn path must be declared
+rather than pass silently. It is asserted empty — `provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts`
+requires that no surface carries it — so adding one is a deliberate, reviewable
+act that fails the contract until justified. It is not a claim that unmanaged
+execution is impossible, only that none is currently admitted.
